story:
Under Prince Abdin's chapter house the rock is full of holes, and Earl Glassalab made them. It is the one earl of the court whose body is not a demon's at all but a crawler's: plated, many-legged and patient, of the same kind as the chthonian crawlers that still nest in the hollow's deep places, and grown to the height of a duke. In the Uncounted Age it dug. It dug under the halls of lords and let them fall in, and the lords who survived learned to pay it not to, and in this way it became the first power of the north-west to grow rich without ever fighting anyone. When Abdin claimed the north-west after the Feast, he paid it the most, and the First Roll wrote it as his earl.

The knights do not like it. A Chthonic Knight is sworn to the deep earth, to hold what is taken and to go down rather than give ground, and Glassalab's whole art is taking the ground out from under things. The chapter house tolerates it because Abdin tells it to, and because the house stands on the earl's tunnels and would fall into them if it were ever displeased. It stands beside the prince's hall with the knights Haag, Gaapoler and Vosoes of Abdin's guard, and the knights stand a little further from it than they stand from each other.

Its present work is the prince's greatest plan. When Director Kobil finishes the Army of Shadows in his chambers above the Gate, the Army will have to march, and every road out of the crossing belongs to Gatekeeper Dommel, who has sworn the Army will find them very long. Glassalab is digging the Army another road. The tunnel runs from the chapter house toward the Director's chambers, under the crossing and not through it, and the imps who have been down it say it is already longer than any road Dommel keeps. Dommel knows. The Gatekeeper is said to have put his ear to the floor of the crossing in the Tenth Roll and listened for a whole dark, and then to have cut a notch in the floor that was not for any mortal.
legend: Glassalab is the giant bug in Prince Abdin's hall in the north-west: an insect body, not a demon, standing next to Chthonic Knights Haag, Gaapoler and Vosoes, with the prince himself under nine hundred units away. Level 71, no script. Clear the three knights of Abdin's guard one at a time first, then pull Glassalab away from the prince's room; you want Abdin last and alone. Its body type is insect, which surprises people who read the bestiary for the first time and expected a demon. Players call it the digger and swear the north-west is full of tunnels it dug. Some say there is a tunnel from Abdin's hall to Director Kobil's chambers above the Gate. Nobody has found it, and nobody who went looking has said where they looked.

loremasterTopic.text: Prince [Abdin]'s earl, a crawler grown to a duke's height, which grew rich in the Uncounted Age by not digging under lords who paid. It is digging the [Army of Shadows] a road from the chapter house to Director [Kobil]'s chambers that does not pass through the Gate.

bookPage: From the report of a Midgard war-band's scout, given at Jordheim: The black knights' house stands on nothing. I put my ear to its floor while the others rested and heard digging under it, steady, the way a beetle digs in rotten wood, and then I heard it stop, and something under the floor listened back. In the hall beside the house there is a thing like a beetle the height of a longhouse, plated and still, and the knights keep their distance from it. I think the house knows that if it ever displeases the beetle it will go down into the dark all at once, and I think the knights know it too.
